audit_findings.title: The earnings anchor predates a completed 40% Colstrip acquisition
audit_findings.magnitude: 592 MW acquired; approximately $48 million annual incremental operating and maintenance costs; six-month 2026 acquisition-related maintenance was $20.3 million and Puget-interest margin was $10.2 million; net owner-earnings effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The acquisition changes recurring revenue, operating costs, maintenance capital and financing costs after the 2025 OE anchor, while the bridge uses the post-acquisition balance sheet.
audit_findings.evidence: In January 2023, and July 2024, we entered into definitive agreements with Avista and Puget, respectively, to acquire their respective interests in Colstrip Units 3 and 4 for $ 0 and completed these acquisitions on January 1, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a possible adjustment. The $73.9 million anchor contains no 2026 acquired operations, although their filed annual operating costs equal about 65% of that anchor. The Puget interests generated positive margin, but Avista recovery was insufficient and the complete maintenance-capital and financing effects are unavailable, so direction is mixed. The scale is reasonably capable of materially changing modeled value.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE from 2026 results, separately tracing Avista and Puget revenue, operating costs, maintenance capital, financing costs, FERC-approved rates, the Ninth Circuit appeal and MPSC recovery; rerun all scenarios on the resulting post-acquisition perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth uses a static denominator despite planned equity issuance
audit_findings.mechanism: Future common issuance increases fully diluted shares and may fund the capital investment underlying forecast aggregate OE growth, reducing OE and value per current share.
audit_findings.evidence: In order to fund South Dakota generation investment equity issuances are expected beginning in 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing says equity issuance is expected beginning in 2027, but provides no amount, price or issuance schedule. No dilution has yet been demonstrated, so this is forward-looking. If issuance funds modeled growth while the denominator remains 62.035506 million shares, per-share value will be overstated.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the equity-financing amount, timing, expected issue prices and associated project-level OE; rerun each growth case with annual fully diluted share counts and financing-consistent OE.

audit_findings.title: A YCGS add-back could erase a real loss of shareholder capital
audit_findings.magnitude: $30.9 million pre-tax capital disallowance, equal to about $0.50 per diluted share and 3.0% of the $1.042 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: If the noncash charge was added back to OE and the related unrecoverable construction spending was also excluded from maintenance capital, the one-time shareholder-capital loss is absent from both OE and the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result, in the fourth quarter of 2025 we recorded a $ 30.9 million non-cash charge for the regulatory disallowance within Operating and maintenance on the Consolidated Statements of Income and a corresponding reduction to Property, plant, and equipment, net on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The $30.9 million economic loss is filed, but the alleged valuation error remains unresolved because the OE adjustment ledger was not supplied. Even if the entire amount were omitted and deducted from equity value, it would reduce base value from $16.80 to about $16.30 per share and would not change the conclusion relative to the $70.78 market price. Reconsideration could also restore some recovery.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE ledger and capital-expenditure classification; ensure the $30.9 million is recognized exactly once, and rerun the bridge if it was omitted. Update the adjustment if the MPSC modifies its order.

audit_findings.title: The bridge omits a separate unrecoverable QF claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $14.877 million present-value liability at 2025-12-31; $11.196 million undiscounted net obligation at 2026-06-30; the filed PV equals about $0.24 per share and 1.4% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Unrecovered QF settlement principal reduces cash available to common equity unless the outflows are already included in forecast OE; interest accretion alone does not settle principal.
audit_findings.evidence: This obligation is reflected in the electric QF liability, which reflects the unrecoverable costs associated with these specific QF contracts per the stipulation.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated, subject to checking whether forecast OE already captures the settlements. Using the larger filed present-value balance, a deduction would reduce base value from $16.80 to about $16.56 per share and cannot change the valuation conclusion relative to the $70.78 price.
audit_findings.action: Trace QF purchases, rate recoveries, liability reductions and cash settlements through OE; if principal outflows are not forecast, deduct the current present-value net liability once and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The standalone NWE denominator ceases to represent the security if the merger closes
audit_findings.magnitude: 0.98 Black Hills share per NWE share; approximately 60.194486 million Black Hills shares based on the filed 61.422945 million NWE shares
audit_findings.mechanism: Closing replaces each standalone NWE share with 0.98 share of the combined parent, requiring combined-company OE, post-merger financing and combined fully diluted shares.
audit_findings.evidence: Pursuant to the Merger Agreement, at the effective time of the Merger, each share of common stock of NorthWestern issued and outstanding as of immediately prior to closing will be converted into the right to receive 0.98 validly issued, fully paid and non-assessable shares of common stock of Black Hills, par value $1.00 per share (Black Hills Common Stock).
audit_findings.explanation: The merger remains pending, so the current AS_FILED standalone denominator has not yet ceased to represent the security. The valuation already identifies year-end 2026 as the rerun trigger. Upon closing, however, the standalone per-share valuation becomes obsolete; the direction cannot be known without valuing Black Hills and the combined company.
audit_findings.action: Maintain separate standalone/no-closing and merger-closing cases; immediately upon closing, replace the standalone model with combined-company OE and bridge analysis and translate value through the 0.98 exchange ratio.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor may retain a nonrecurring tax release
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.4 million filed benefit, equal to 14.1% of the $73.9 million anchor; if fully embedded, the computed base-value overstatement is about $146.1 million or $2.36 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring tax and accrued-interest release increases 2025 net income and, if retained in anchor OE, is capitalized through every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Income tax expense for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, includes a $10.4 million benefit related to a reduction in our unrecognized tax benefits, inclusive of $3.0 million of previously accrued interest ($7.4 million net of interest).
audit_findings.explanation: The release and its magnitude are demonstrated, but retention in the OE anchor is an unresolved possibility because the adjustment ledger was not supplied. If unremoved, its capitalization would materially overstate modeled value; the filed 2026 effective tax rate of 16.3% also confirms that the 2025 release is not a sustainable tax component.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the 2025 OE reconciliation for removal of the full $10.4 million release, including $3.0 million of accrued interest; if retained, reduce anchor OE accordingly and rerun every scenario using a sustainable tax burden while preserving recurring regulatory tax effects.
